chunks: Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bakr al-Khuri in Naysabur narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad the Jurist al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Juybari al-Shaybani narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, had decreed the destinies and arranged the plans two thousand years before He created Adam.

key_terms.التَّدَابِيرَ: The plans or arrangements (plural of tadbir)
key_terms.الْمَقَادِيرَ: The destinies or decrees (plural of qadar)

ai.seo_question: What does Shia theology say about the timing of divine decree relative to the creation of Adam?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* anchors the Shia doctrine of divine decree (*al-maqadir*) in the pre-eternal knowledge of Allah, specifying a two-thousand-year period before Adam’s creation to illustrate the temporal manifestation of divine planning (*al-tadabir*). It highlights the balance between Allah’s absolute sovereignty and the reality of trials (*fitan*) and sustenance (*rizq*), affirming that all events are meticulously orchestrated by the Divine Will. This context reinforces the Shia understanding of *adl* (divine justice) within the framework of *jabr* (divine power), distinguishing it from mere fatalism.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 22. Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bakr al-Khuri said in Naysabur that Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Khuri said: Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad the Jurist in al-Khuri said: Ahmad ibn `Abd Allah al-Juybari al-Shaybani said, on the authority of `Ali ibn Musa alRida, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of `Ali (AS) that The Messenger of Allah (SA) said: “
Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, had decreed and planned everything two thousand years before He created Adam (AS).”
